headline: Maui County Council Meeting

meeting.summary: The council advanced limits on new West Maui pools, approved a Lānaʻi housing land lease, and sent a hotel-district plan to planning commissions.
meeting.recap: The council voted 9–0 to adopt a resolution honoring a kumu hula (hula teacher).[[0:30:38]] Two committee reports passed 9–0, including a $22,409,000 loan item for Lahaina wastewater plant upgrades.[[1:54:09]] The council voted 9–0 to grant a ground lease for an affordable housing project on Lānaʻi.[[2:08:53]] A council member said a FEMA email warned that 700 households may need to move out by February 28th.[[2:14:32]] Bill 4 moves $5 million from the Open Space Fund to a grant for the Lahaina Community Land Trust.[[2:18:10]] Bills for a safe parking program and a $40,000 grant passed first reading 9–0.[[2:24:16]] Bill 8 adds $13,137 for a Lahaina homecoming event.[[2:26:11]] Resolution 25-230 sends a bill creating H3 and H4 hotel districts to the Lānaʻi, Maui and Molokaʻi planning commissions.[[2:48:05]] The new districts would let some apartment-zoned properties keep transient vacation rentals (short-term rentals).[[2:48:33]]
decided: The council approved the recommendations in two budget committee reports, including the Lahaina wastewater loan item.
The council approved two one-year lease extensions on county-owned land.
The council approved a ground lease for a long-term affordable housing project on Lānaʻi.
Bill 1, on the water availability policy for subdivision construction plans, was sent to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
Bills 9 and 10, budget changes for water systems and technology, were sent to the Budget, Finance and Economic Development Committee.
Bills 184, 186 through 191, and 193 passed final reading.
Bill 192, updating terms for a resiliency hub, passed final reading.
Bill 194, on County Council vacancies in office, passed final reading.
The council filed an older Lānaʻi ground lease resolution that Resolution 26-4 replaced.
meeting.next: A council member said she is drafting shoreline language for all zoning districts, due by the end of the month.

issues.oneLine: The council approved a ground lease for a long-term affordable housing project on Lānaʻi.
issues.why: A council member said the lease advances the goal of long-term affordable housing on Lānaʻi.
issues.next: The developer said a state funding application process starts in February, and land control is a key part of it.
issues.brief: The council filed an older Lānaʻi lease resolution because Resolution 26-4 replaced it.[[#1]]

issues.oneLine: The council moved $5 million to a grant for the Lahaina Community Land Trust.
issues.why: A testifier said many lots may go up for sale once the fire settlement is signed, and the money helps keep them out of investor hands.
issues.brief: The testifier said 25 parcels have been protected in just over two years.[[#1]] The event is expected to cost $300,000, with the rest paid by private donations.[[#2]]
